_readme: Scholar aliases: how one paper written two ways becomes one row (README §18).
`tools/fetch-scholar.mjs` joins the Google Scholar profile to
data/publications.json on the title, and it is good at the small
differences — a hyphen, a vowel, British against American spelling, a title
Scholar truncated. It is deliberately not good at large ones, because a
matcher loose enough to join two genuinely different papers would put the
wrong citation count under the wrong title and never say so.
So the rest is here, by hand. Each key is the title exactly as GOOGLE
SCHOLAR writes it; each value is the title exactly as data/publications.json
writes it. The fetcher prints every entry it could not join and their
citation counts, so this file is written by reading that report.
A truncated Scholar title may be used as the key: write what Scholar shows
and end it with the same ellipsis character.
Nothing here is required. With this file missing or empty every unambiguous
paper still gets its badge; the awkward ones simply go without.
